function: Transceiver design for over-the-air aggregation of local soft predictions in federated distillation: device transmit power, PS estimator scalars and receive beamforming, maximizing the convergence rate (p. 1, p. 3).
system: PS with 5 antennas (5 to 100 in sweep), 50 single-antenna devices (100 for ViT), analog over-the-air aggregation, block fading; no RIS; 915 MHz (p. 7-10).
method: Federated distillation: devices train ResNet-18 or ViT-B/16 by gradient descent with a soft-prediction distillation regularizer; transceiver by closed form and semidefinite relaxation, not learned (p. 3, p. 7-10).
data_channel: Simulated IID Gaussian small-scale fading with path loss exponent 4; FMNIST, CIFAR-10 (IID and Dirichlet non-IID), Oxford Flowers (ViT) datasets (p. 7, p. 10).
test_conditions: Separate training runs, tested on held-out sets: FMNIST 400 rounds, CIFAR-10 200 rounds; IID and non-IID splits; sweeps of distillation weight, antennas, CSI error (p. 7-10).
baselines: Error-free FD, error-free FedAvg, uniform beamforming, orthogonal channels, MSE minimization [11], sparsified over-the-air FL [9], pruned and quantized over-the-air FL [15], digital OFDMA FD [38] (p. 9-11).
metrics: Global testing accuracy versus rounds, total time and uplink time; analytical convergence gap; training and distillation loss; eigenvalues of the relaxed beamformer; run time per round (p. 7-10).
complexity: Algorithm 1 per round O(N^3 + M) (interior point plus eigendecomposition O(N^2.376)); measured average run time 0.12 s per round (p. 7).
openness: none; no code or data link, only public FMNIST, CIFAR-10 and Oxford Flowers datasets (p. 7, p. 10).
q1_support: p. 7: "The channel coefficient is modelled by the small scale fading multiplied by the square root of the path loss": IID Gaussian fading with free-space path loss; custom simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 7: "we further devise the following IID and non-IID dataset settings for the CIFAR-10 dataset"; p. 8: sweeps of distillation weight, antennas and CSI error; each run trains its own model. No model is tested in an unseen scenario, band or dataset.
q3_support: p. 9: "(Over-the-air FD with) MSE Minimization [11]" and "(Over-the-air FL with) 90%-Sparse Rate [9]" are earlier published designs, with "the proposed algorithm achieves a higher performance than the MSE minimization benchmark" (testing accuracy); "Uniform Beamforming" is the non-learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 7: "the overall computational complexity of obtaining the optimal" transceivers per FD round is O(N^3 + M); footnote 4: "Algorithm 1 is 0.12s" average run time per round. Cost of the transceiver design, not the model size.
q5_support: p. 7: "We simulate an image classification task on ResNet-18 over the FMNIST and CIFAR-10 dataset": public datasets of the learning task only; channels are simulated; no code or data link is given in the paper.
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. Included as FL over the air: the aggregated quantity is the per-class soft predictions (federated distillation) rather than model parameters, summed over the air; the learned element is the model trained across devices (ResNet-18, ViT-B/16). The transceiver is closed form plus SDR, not learned. The PS has several antennas, so the single-antenna rule does not apply; no RIS (reference [25] only). q2: the ViT-B/16 fine-tuning on Oxford Flowers (p. 10) is a separate run, not a test in new conditions. q3 uses published over-the-air FL and FD designs compared on testing accuracy and uplink time.
